reason: Reproduced, and nothing documented prevents it. The merge setup covers only log.md (union) and decisions.md (the jarl-decisions driver); .jarl/issues/ has no driver, and two files with different slugs never conflict, so the documented merge-driver flags change nothing. A clone gets no local driver configuration, and its first write adds none, because the setup runs only when .gitattributes is missing (jarl-lib.mjs:206-207). The numbering reads this checkout and its worktrees only (highestAcrossWorktrees, jarl-lib.mjs:1493-1500), and the guard on new refuses only a linked worktree (jarl-lib.mjs:1523). The docs say numbers never collide because the write lock hands them out (SKILL.md:99, references/jarl.md:45, references/repositories.md:40), and that lock lives in one checkout (references/record.md, The write lock). One correction makes it worse than written: set and every other move write the number into log.md, and the log is the record, so a move on 2 moves both issues numbered 2. After set 2 dropped, list shows both dropped while the second file still reads open. verify then reports the second file as disagreeing with the log and advises writing the log state into it, which would drop an issue nobody dropped. verify is clean only until the first move, and it never names the shared number. Two branches of one checkout that each file an issue end the same way.
run: Clones a and b of one committed loop. (a) new "second on A", commit. (b) new "second on B", commit. (b) git fetch; git $(jarl.mjs merge-driver flags) merge --no-ff origin/main → "Auto-merging .jarl/log.md", no conflict. ls .jarl/issues → 2-second-on-a.md 2-second-on-b.md. list --all → two rows numbered 2. verify → "verify: clean", exit 0. show 2 → "# 2 · second on A"; show 2-second-on-b → "no such issue". set 2 in-progress --branch jarl/2-x --worker w1 → only 2-second-on-a.md changed; list --all shows both in-progress; verify → 4 findings on 2 ("Status reads open in the file and in-progress in the log, which is the record — to follow the log, write …"), exit 2. set 2 dropped → list shows both dropped; 2-second-on-b.md still reads open. One checkout, branches x and y from main, new on each → "filed 2 · 2-on-x.md" and "filed 2 · 2-on-y.md"; both merged into main with the flags → no conflict, list shows two issues numbered 2, verify clean.
correction: Add to the claim: every move of the number lands on both issues in the record (log.md), so list, resume and the done gate treat the second issue as moved too. verify reports the second file only as a header that disagrees with the log, and its advice would copy the wrong state into it. The cause also covers two branches of one checkout, not only separate clones.

reason: Reproduced as written, for committed and permanent loops alike. init creates .jarl/issues/ (jarl-lib.mjs:1357) and writes no placeholder, so git ls-files lists no issues/. In the clone, verify, status, resume, list and next all pass, because the readers check that the directory exists (jarl-lib.mjs:1497, 5062); only new reads it with readdirSync and no check (jarl-lib.mjs:1562). init refuses in the clone because a live loop exists, so no command repairs it; ask and decide work. No doc names the case, and the clone test in tests/one-store.test.mjs files its issue before cloning. Medium is honest: new is blocked with a raw error, nothing is lost, and mkdir .jarl/issues gets past it once someone reads the message.
run: git init a; init "g" --committed; commit. git ls-files .jarl → .gitattributes .gitignore decisions.md goal.md log.md. git clone a b. (b) verify → "verify: clean"; status, resume, list --all, next → exit 0. new "first in a fresh clone" → "ENOENT: no such file or directory, scandir '<b>/.jarl/issues'", exit 1, nothing written. init "g" --committed → ".jarl/ already exists here with a live loop". decide s1 → "decided s1"; ask → "asked a-1". The same with init --permanent → the same ENOENT.
